indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the two words are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: An uncle is cross about the pen, perhaps one he lent and lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like it means 'concerning', but it tells you to rearrange UNCLE SORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen is a fenced area for animals, which is a kind of enclosed space.

definitions.meaning: someone's good standing in the eyes of others, as in making a reputation for oneself
everyone is given one at birth, the word by which they are called

explanation.definitionFit: A good name is a reputation, and everyone has a personal label they are called by.

clue.text: Left ale spilt on the sheet

indicators.note: spilt suggests the beer is splashed about, so its letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has knocked over a pint and the beer has run all over a sheet of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilt' tells you to rearrange the letters of LEFT ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaflet is a single printed sheet of paper handed out to people.

clue.text: Rose let down by her boy friend?

definitions.meaning: rose is the past tense of rise, to get up onto one's feet

definitions.text: let down by her boy friend?
definitions.meaning: a girl whose date never turns up has been left waiting by him

explanation.surface: A girl called Rose is disappointed by her boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: Rose reads as a girl's name but is the verb 'got up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Having risen means getting onto one's feet; being failed by a date who never arrives is the idiom for it too.

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of soldiers
RE is the Royal Engineers, another body of soldiers

explanation.surface: Combining two kinds of soldiers is an unusual thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: Two British army units: the Royal Artillery (RA) and the Royal Engineers (RE) put together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare is seldom found, so it is out of the ordinary.

parts.note: a run of victories, read jokingly as a naked dash by someone who is winning

explanation.walkthrough: To streak is to run naked in public, so a victorious naked runner is having a run of successes.
explanation.definitionFit: A run of consecutive victories, with streaking meaning running naked as the joke.

clue.text: Is such a diet less stiff?

definitions.text: Is such a diet less stiff?

parts.words: Is such a diet less stiff?
parts.note: starch both stiffens laundry and is a carbohydrate in food, so a low-carbohydrate diet is jokingly less stiff

explanation.walkthrough: Starch stiffens collars as well as being a food carbohydrate, which gives the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes food with less of the carbohydrate found in bread and potatoes, used for slimming diets.

clue.text: The most popular member of the company?

definitions.text: The most popular member of the company?

parts.words: The most popular member of the company?
parts.note: read as a staff member everyone likes best, and as a well-liked choice in general, a company being a business

explanation.walkthrough: A firm is a company, so the person best liked at a business is its favourite in two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A strongly preferred choice that people stick with, punned as the best-liked person at a business.

parts.note: a rod or perch is an old unit of length, five and a half yards

indicators.note: broken means smashed into pieces, so the letters of the stick are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fishing rod and a walking cane might both be broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges CANE into ANCE; PERCH (a rod, an old measure of length) comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Perchance is an old-fashioned word for possibly.

clue.text: Maniacal road speed from a reckless guy

indicators.note: maniacal suggests wild, crazed behaviour, so the letters are jumbled madly

explanation.surface: Driving at maniacal speed on the road is typical of a reckless fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maniacal' tells you to rearrange ROAD SPEED.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a bold, lawless outlaw who takes wild risks.

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the run of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bird that can be seen in northern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'Northern' and the start of 'Europe'.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, a crossword favourite among birds.

parts.note: pleased means glad, happy

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of enemy

explanation.surface: The enemy commander is pleased to have made a clearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A glade is an open space in a forest.

clue.text: Available when the price is about right

indicators.note: is about means goes around, so the charge wraps the letter for right

parts.note: a fee is a price charged

explanation.surface: Something is on offer when the price is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Something free is at liberty or not taken, so it is available for use.
Funny means both peculiar and comic.

clue.text: Without interest, without debts to bring upon oneself

indicators.note: the second without means minus, so one piece is taken away from the other

parts.note: someone without interest lacks curiosity, which is to be incurious
IOUs are written promises to pay, so debts

explanation.surface: Being free of both interest charges and debts.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Without' belongs to the phrase meaning incurious; the second is the deletion signal, removing IOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a cost or penalty is to bring it on yourself through your actions.

definitions.meaning: to lead or guide, as a guide leads a party round a museum
to carry oneself in a certain manner, the reflexive verb sense

explanation.definitionFit: Conduct means to guide others and, used of oneself, to act in a given manner.

clue.text: Fight but do not hit below the belt

definitions.text: do not hit below the belt
definitions.meaning: a playful instruction to aim punches high rather than low

explanation.walkthrough: PUNCH-UP is British slang for a brawl; the second reading tells a boxer to aim high.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl is a punch-up in British slang, and punching up means aiming blows high.

clue.text: Lack the cause of that fonder feeling

definitions.meaning: a want or not being present

definitions.text: the cause of that fonder feeling
definitions.meaning: refers to the proverb that being away makes the heart grow fonder

explanation.definitionFit: Absence is the state of being missing, and the proverb says it makes the heart grow fonder.

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
plain means clear, evident

explanation.surface: An account that is no longer clear.
explanation.definitionFit: To account for something is to give the reasons for it, the verb sense here.

clue.text: Bribe with French coin back in grim surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings says the grim word encloses the coin

parts.note: dour means grim, stern

indicators.note: back means the coin's letters are read the other way

parts.note: the ecu is an old French coin

explanation.surface: A bribe is paid back in French money in grim surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: The ecu is an old French coin, here read backwards; 'surroundings' means the grim word wraps round it. 'Bribe' sounds harsh, but a douceur is a polite word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A douceur is a sweetener given to win favour, a polite word for a backhander.

parts.note: does is slang for cheats or swindles
kin means family, relatives

explanation.surface: A family business that cheats people in the leather trade.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'do' someone is British slang for to cheat them.
explanation.definitionFit: Doeskin is soft leather made from the hide of a female deer.

definitions.meaning: a person with odd, amusing habits
a single member of a deck used for games like poker or bridge

explanation.definitionFit: An odd character is called a card, and a deck of playing cards is a pack.

parts.note: to be up on a subject is to know it well
a set is a group

explanation.definitionFit: An upset is a surprise defeat of a favourite.

indicators.note: sounded says it is the spoken form of the word that counts

parts.note: rude means impolite

explanation.surface: Someone regretted what they said because it came across as rude.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue is to be sorry for, so rued means was sorry about.

definitions.meaning: to retain or hang on to something
the strongest central tower of a castle, its last stronghold

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold the fort' reads as a stock phrase but splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep is to retain, and the keep is a castle's inner stronghold.

parts.note: dim means obscure, faint

explanation.surface: An obscure coin from the eastern United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A dime is a ten-cent piece in the US.

parts.note: a rider sitting on a horse with no saddle

explanation.definitionFit: A circus or rodeo performer who rides a horse with no saddle.

parts.note: the Open is a famous golf championship
ended means finished

explanation.surface: A golf tournament finished with no clear winner decided.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open is the British Open golf championship.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-ended arrangement has no fixed limit or final decision settled.
